σεαυτοῦ.der: genitive case from G4571 (σέ) and G846 (αὐτός), also dative case of the same, , and accusative case , likewise contracted , , and , respectively;
σεαυτοῦ.as:
σεαυτοῦ, -ῆς, -οῦ
(in NT not contracted, σαυτοῦ, as in Att..),
reflex. prop. of 2nd pers. sing., used only in gen., dat. and acc.
(of, to) thyself: Mt 4:6, Jo 8:13, I Ti 4:16, al. (In Hellenistic, the pl. is ἑαυτῶν (q.v.), not ὑμῶν αὐτῶν as in Attic, v. Bl., § 13, 1.) †

σεληνιάζομαι.long: I am a lunatic, am moonstruck, epileptic.
σεληνιάζομαι.der: middle voice or passive from a presumed derivative of G4582 (σελήνη);
σεληνιάζομαι.as:
*† σεληνιάζω
(< σελήνη),
act, in Manetho (Carm., 4, 81), in NT depon. -ομαι,
to be moonstruck, i.e. epileptic (epilepsy being supposed to be influenced by the moon): Mt 4:2417:15.†

σεισμός.long: a shaking (as an earthquake); a storm.
σεισμός.sd: a commotion, i.e. (of the air) a gale, (of the ground) an earthquake
σεισμός.as:
σεισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< σείω), [in LXX chiefly for רַעַשׁ ;]
a shaking, commotion, as a tempest at sea: Mt 8:24; esp. an earthquake: Mt 24:727:5428:2, Mk 13:8, Lk 21:11, Ac 16:26, Re 6:128:511:13, 1916:18.†

σέβομαι.der: middle voice of an apparently primary verb;
σέβομαι.as:
σέβω
[in LXX (chiefly for יָרֵא, Jos 4:24, al.) and NT always mid., σέβομαι, exc. IV Mac 5:24 ;]
to worship: c. acc. pers., Mt 15:9, Mk 7:7, Ac 18:1319:27; σεβόμενος τ. θεόν, Ac 16:1418:7; σεβόμενοι (σ. προσήλυτοι, σ. Ἕλληνες), devout, Ac 13:43, 5017:4, 17 (cf. προσήλυτος).†

σείω.long: I shake; fig: I agitate, stir up.
σείω.sd: to rock (vibrate, properly, sideways or to and fro), i.e. (generally) to agitate (in any direction; cause to tremble); figuratively, to throw into a tremor (of fear or concern)
σείω.as:
σείω
[in LXX chiefly for רעשׁ ;]
to shake, move to and fro: τ. γῆν, He 12:26(LXX); pass., ἡ γῆ, Mt 27:51(LXX); συκῆ, Re 6:13. Metaph., to agitate, stir up, with fear or some other emotion: Mt 21:1028:4 (cf. ἀνα-, δια-, κατα-σείω).†

σελήνη.sd: probably akin to the alternate of G138 (αἱρέομαι), through the idea of attractiveness); the moon
σελήνη.as:
σελήνη, -ης, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for יָרֵחַ (Ge 37:9, al.), also for לְבָנָה; (Ca 6:9 (10), Is 24:23א, 30:26) ;]
the moon: Mt 24:29, Mk 13:24, Lk 21:25, Ac 2:20(LXX), I Co 15:41, Re 6:128:1212:121:23.†

Σερούχ.as:
Σερούχ (Rec. Σαρ-), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. שְׂרוּג),
Serug: Lk 3:35.†

Σελεύκεια.long: Seleucia, on the Syrian coast, the harbor of Syrian Antioch.
Σελεύκεια.as:
Σελευκία (Rec. -εύκεια),
Seleucia, a city of Syria: Ac 13:4.†

Σέργιος.long: Sergius, the middle (gentile) name of the proconsul of Cyprus.

σέβασμα.long: an object of worship or veneration.
σέβασμα.sd: something adored, i.e. an object of worship (god, altar, etc)
σέβασμα.as:
** σέβασμα, -τος, τό
(< σεβάζομαι), [in LXX: Wi 14:2015:17, Da TH Bel 1:27 * ;]
an object of worship: Ac 17:23, II Th 2:4.†

Σεβαστός.long: (official Greek equivalent of Augustus), venerated, august, a title of the Roman emperors; hence secondarily: Augustan, imperial.
Σεβαστός.sd: venerable (august), i.e. (as noun) a title of the Roman Emperor, or (as adjective) imperial
Σεβαστός.as:
* σεβαστός, -ή, -όν (σεβάζομαι)
1.reverend, august.
2. In late writers, with reference to the Roman Imperial name;
(a)ὁ Σ., Augustus, i.e. the Roman Emperor: Ac 25:21, 25;
(b)Augustan: σπείρα σ., Ac 27:1 (See further, Deiss., BS, 218.) †

σεβάζομαι.long: I worship, stand in awe of.
σεβάζομαι.der: middle voice from a derivative of G4576 (σέβομαι);
σεβάζομαι.as:
** σεβάζομαι
(< σέβας, reverential awe), [in Aq.: Ho 10:5 * ;]
1.to fear (Hom).
2. In later writers, = σέβομαι, to worship: Ro 1:25

σεμνός.as:
σεμνός, -ή, -όν
(< σέβομαι), [in LXX: Pr 6:88:615:26(נָגִיד,נֹעַם), II Mac 6:11, 6:288:15, IV Mac 5:367:1517:5 * ;]
1.reverend, august, venerable, in cl. of the gods and also of human beings.
2.grave, serious; of persons: I Ti 3:8, 11, Tit 2:2; of things: Phl 4:8 (v. Tr., Syn., § xcii; Cremer, 37; MM, xxii).†

σεμνότης.as:
** σεμνότης, -ητος, ἡ
(< σεμνός), [in LXX: II Mac 3:12 * ;]
gravity: I Ti 2:23:4 (Vg. castitas, cf. Soph., Lex., and Zorell, s.v.), Tit 2:7.†

σειρά.sd: akin to G138 (αἱρέομαι)); a chain (as binding or drawing)
σειρά.der: probably from G4951 (σύρω) through its congener (to fasten;
σειρά.as:
σειρά, -ᾶς, ἡ
[in LXX: Jg 16:13, 14, 19 (מַחְלָפוֺת), Pr 5:22 (חֶבֶל) * ;]
1.
(a)a cord;
(b)a chain (cf. Pr., l.c.): σειραὶ ζόφου, II Pe 2:4, Rec., R, mg. (v.s. σειρός).
2.a lock of hair (Jg, ll. c.).†

σεμίδαλις.as:
σεμίδαλις, -εως, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for סֹלֶת ;]
fine wheaten flour: Re 18:13.†
